session.question: How do energy resourses and renewable energy in mining together help with environmental sustainability and sustainable development, and what good effects are said about using renewable energy in mining for sustainability?
session.answer:
Energy resources in mining support environmental sustainability by enabling lower-impact power supply for extraction and processing, especially when mines are far from urban grids and rely heavily on fossil fuels. In this context, renewable energy is presented as a substitute that reduces dependence on fossil fuels, lowers emissions, and supports sustainable development goals (SDGs) through strategic planning. The literature also notes that mining supplies minerals needed for low-carbon technologies, so improving energy use in mining is part of the broader transition toward sustainability. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1, ivic2021driversofsustainability chunk 1)

The good effects reported for renewable energy adoption in mining include reduced environmental pollution, lower operating costs, creation of new jobs, increased knowledge in mining regions, and promotion of a circular economy. These benefits are described as improving sustainable development indicators. The SWOT analysis in the study concludes that strengths and opportunities of renewable energy outweigh weaknesses and threats, supporting aggressive adoption. Challenges remain, including high upfront investment, lack of skilled labor, and maintenance costs. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1)

More generally, the context indicates that renewable energy use in mining can positively affect environmental sustainability and sustainable development by reducing fossil-fuel dependence and mitigating negative environmental impacts, thereby supporting low-carbon transitions and SDG alignment. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1, ivic2021driversofsustainability chunk 1)

session.context:
pqac-fa349d0e: The paper says mining energy demand is largely met by fossil fuels because mines are often far from cities, so integrating renewable energy is presented as an effective way to reduce this dependence. It examines how renewable energy adoption in mining supports Sustainable Development Goals through strategic planning (SWOT). Reported benefits include lower environmental pollution, reduced operating costs, creation of new jobs, increased knowledge in mining areas, and promotion of a circular economy. These effects are described as improving sustainable development indicators. The study also notes that strengths and opportunities of renewable energy in mining outweigh weaknesses and threats, supporting an aggressive strategy for adoption.
From Mahdi Pouresmaieli, Mohammad Ataei, Ali Nouri Qarahasanlou, and Abbas Barabadi. Integration of renewable energy and sustainable development with strategic planning in the mining industry. Results in Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rineng.2023.101412, doi:10.1016/j.rineng.2023.101412.

pqac-e851de2d: The excerpt reports that integrating renewable energy in mining can support sustainable development by creating new jobs, reducing environmental pollution, increasing knowledge in mining areas, fostering a circular economy, and lowering operating costs. Environmentally, it is described as a way to reduce the fossil-fuel dependence of mines, which are often far from urban areas and highly reliant on fossil fuels. The paper states that renewable energy use can positively affect sustainable development indicators, and that its strengths and opportunities outweigh weaknesses and threats in the SWOT analysis. It also notes challenges such as high investment, lack of skilled labor, and maintenance costs.
From Mahdi Pouresmaieli, Mohammad Ataei, Ali Nouri Qarahasanlou, and Abbas Barabadi. Integration of renewable energy and sustainable development with strategic planning in the mining industry. Results in Engineering, 2023. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rineng.2023.101412, doi:10.1016/j.rineng.2023.101412.

pqac-710707a7: The excerpt says mining, especially coal mining, supports economic growth and development, and that coal is described as a viable renewable energy source with large deposits in Thar. However, the study finds Sindh Engro coal mining is potentially unsustainable environmentally. It reports emissions of toxic gases such as methane, carbon dioxide, and sulfur during operations, and negative impacts on the atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere, and lithosphere. Human needs and interests are generally positively affected, but human health and safety are exceptions. It suggests cleaner technologies, plantation, and ecological restoration to reduce pollution.
From Muhammad Mohsin, Zhu Qiang, Sobia Naseem, Muddassar Sarfraz, and Larisa Ivaşcu. Mining industry impact on environmental sustainability, economic growth, social interaction, and public health: an application of semi-quantitative mathematical approach. Processes, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.3390/pr9060972, doi:10.3390/pr9060972.

pqac-44f0d7b9: The excerpt explains that mining companies reported on environment-related topics including energy use, but for most companies air emissions, water use, and energy usage increased, while there was an absence of improvement in renewable energy utilization. The paper notes that mining provides minerals needed for low-carbon technology and links sustainability reporting to the SDGs, but also says companies did not give a comprehensive explanation of how mining contributes to the SDGs. It highlights that renewable energy use in mining was one of the areas lacking progress, suggesting it is important for environmental sustainability and sustainable development, especially in reducing negative impacts and supporting low-carbon transitions.
From Anđela Ivic, Nína M. Saviolidis, and Lára Jóhannsdóttir. Drivers of sustainability practices and contributions to sustainable development evident in sustainability reports of european mining companies. Discover Sustainability, 2021. URL: https://doi.org/10.1007/s43621-021-00025-y, doi:10.1007/s43621-021-00025-y.

pqac-40987edf: The excerpt discusses lithium brine mining in the Andean Altiplano and its links to sustainability. It says the extraction of lithium, important for the low-carbon economy and SDGs like clean energy and climate action, can strongly affect geodiversity, hydrology, biodiversity, ecosystem services, and indigenous communities. These changes influence all SDGs except SDG 14. The paper also notes that sustainable management could mobilize human, physical, financial, and technological resources to advance the SDGs, while poor management may cause ecosystem collapse, environmental degradation, inequality, conflict, and displacement. It emphasizes that lithium brine mining can both impede and advance sustainable development.
From Eline S. Rentier, Carina Hoorn, and A.C. Seijmonsbergen. Lithium brine mining affects geodiversity and sustainable development goals. Renewable and Sustainable Energy Reviews, 2024. URL: https://doi.org/10.1016/j.rser.2024.114642, doi:10.1016/j.rser.2024.114642.

contexts.context: The excerpt is about industrialization and environmental sustainability in Africa, not mining specifically. It finds that manufacturing value added has a negative and significant effect on environmental sustainability, but when manufacturing is combined with renewable energy consumption, the effect becomes positive, indicating that renewable energy can support industrial growth while sustaining the environment. Non-renewable energy shows mixed results: positive in fixed effects but negative in GLS, with the warning that fossil fuels like natural gas may support manufacturing in the short run but become unsustainable over time. The paper recommends renewable energy as the main industrial energy source for sustainable industrialization.

contexts.context: The excerpt discusses lithium brine mining in the Andean Altiplano and its sustainability implications, rather than renewable energy use in mining directly. It reports that lithium extraction affects geodiversity across all essential variables, especially hydrology through depletion, pollution, and changing hydrodynamics. These environmental changes have consequences for biodiversity, ecosystem services, and indigenous communities, and can influence all SDGs except SDG 14. The paper also notes a trade-off: sustainable management could mobilize resources to advance SDGs, while poor management may cause ecosystem collapse, irreversible degradation, inequality, conflict, and displacement. No specific benefits of renewable energy use in mining are described.

session.formatted_answer:
Question: How do energy resourses and renewable energy in mining together help with environmental sustainability and sustainable development, and what good effects are said about using renewable energy in mining for sustainability?

Energy resources in mining support environmental sustainability by enabling lower-impact power supply for extraction and processing, especially when mines are far from urban grids and rely heavily on fossil fuels. In this context, renewable energy is presented as a substitute that reduces dependence on fossil fuels, lowers emissions, and supports sustainable development goals (SDGs) through strategic planning. The literature also notes that mining supplies minerals needed for low-carbon technologies, so improving energy use in mining is part of the broader transition toward sustainability. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1, ivic2021driversofsustainability chunk 1)

The good effects reported for renewable energy adoption in mining include reduced environmental pollution, lower operating costs, creation of new jobs, increased knowledge in mining regions, and promotion of a circular economy. These benefits are described as improving sustainable development indicators. The SWOT analysis in the study concludes that strengths and opportunities of renewable energy outweigh weaknesses and threats, supporting aggressive adoption. Challenges remain, including high upfront investment, lack of skilled labor, and maintenance costs. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1)

More generally, the context indicates that renewable energy use in mining can positively affect environmental sustainability and sustainable development by reducing fossil-fuel dependence and mitigating negative environmental impacts, thereby supporting low-carbon transitions and SDG alignment. (pouresmaieli2023integrationofrenewable chunk 1, ivic2021driversofsustainability chunk 1)
